questions.q: How does Bloom describe empathy's flaw in lesson 1?
a: It is only found in humans
questions.why: Lesson 1 says our empathy is biased and we don't realize it.

questions.q: What example shows empathy's bias toward nearby tragedies?
a: Sandy Hook, versus Syrian children's deaths
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts reactions to Sandy Hook and Syria.

questions.q: How can empathy lead to bad decisions, per lesson 2?
a: It can favor short-term fixes over long-term good
questions.why: Lesson 2 offers the example of giving a crying child a sucker.

questions.q: What problem occurs in some Cambodian orphanages?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says some pocket the money.

questions.q: What does Bloom suggest instead of empathy?
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends helping people more logically.
